title: Jesus Is Praying for Your Faith
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: Faith is a gift we ask for, and Jesus himself is praying that our faith will not fail.
exhortation: My question this morning is, how's your faith? Are you struggling in your faith? Is doubt dominating? Are you going through a season? How do we as believers fight back against doubt and fear?

Well, faith isn't something we manufacture on our own or work harder at. Faith is something we receive as a gift from the Lord. So we start by asking. We go to God in prayer and ask him to increase our faith, to strengthen our faith. Pray that God would do this for you.
Remember that it isn't how big our faith is, it's who our faith is in. That's why Jesus says that faith the size of a mustard seed is sufficient.

And remember that Jesus is interceding for you. You say, "I don't even know if I can pray. I don't know if my prayers are effective." Well, think about this: Jesus is praying for you. Do you think Jesus' prayers are effective? I think they are. When the disciples said, "Lord, increase our faith," Jesus told Peter, "I have prayed for you that your faith may not fail. And when you have turned again, strengthen your brothers."

So remember that our faith is not something we put on our back and charge up the hill with. It's something that carries us up the hill. Faith is the vantage point from which we see all the wondrous mercies of God. Faith is like the cliff above the fog that lets us see all the goodness of God. It's the rock on which we stand, and that is a sure thing.

So are you standing on your own works this morning? Are you feeling like you can't see the goodness of God? Ask Jesus for faith. Pray for faith. And remember that Jesus is praying for you, and his prayers are most certainly answered.
prayer: Jesus, thank you that you are my advocate, interceding on my behalf. Lord, you speak with an effectiveness that I can't muster up. I can't conjure it up. I can't make it happen. I can't pray hard enough. Christ is mine forevermore. Lord, let that be my song today, my prayer.

Reveal wherever we are putting our trust and hope in ourselves, in our strength, in what we do. Fix our eyes on your completed work, the finished work on the cross for us, your blood shed, and the work you are doing now, interceding for us. May it fill our gaze. In Jesus' name, amen.
